title: Best Tires for a RAM 1500 in Calgary
body_html:
The RAM 1500 is one of Calgary's most popular trucks, and picking the right tires matters more than most owners realize. Your tire choice affects fuel economy, ride quality, towing confidence, and whether you stay on the road when Deerfoot gets slick in late October. Here's what you need to know to get the right fitment without the run-around.

The short version

  • Most RAM 1500s take 265–285-width tires in 17-, 18-, or 20-inch diameters — check your door jamb sticker for the exact OEM spec
  • For year-round Calgary driving, an LT-rated all-season highway tire handles the majority of conditions
  • For serious winter confidence, a dedicated winter tire with the 3-Peak Mountain Snowflake symbol is the right call — all-season is not the same thing
  • If you tow or haul regularly, don't downgrade your load range from what the truck came with
  • Prince Tires carries RAM 1500 fitments in multiple brands and price points, with same-day installation and a Price Match Guarantee

What tire sizes fit a RAM 1500?

The RAM 1500 has been built across dozens of trims and years, so there is no single answer. Common factory sizes include:

  • 265/70R17 — base and entry-level trims with 17-inch wheels
  • 275/60R20 — Laramie, Limited, and higher-end trims
  • 275/65R18 — mid-range configurations
  • 285/65R18 and 285/60R20 — TRX, Sport, and off-road packages

Your door jamb sticker has the exact OEM spec. Start there — width, aspect ratio, and wheel diameter all need to match your rim. The load index and speed rating should meet or exceed the original. If you're not sure what you're looking at, bring the sticker info when you call or use our tire finder tool to narrow it down.

All-season tires for the RAM 1500

If you want one set of tires that handles Calgary's dry summer runs, gravel roads, and light early-season snow, a quality all-season LT tire covers the job. A few things to keep in mind when shopping:

LT vs P-metric: Many RAM 1500s leave the factory on P-metric tires, which are fine for regular driving. If you tow a trailer or regularly carry a loaded bed, stepping up to an LT-rated tire makes sense — it adds load capacity and stiffer sidewalls that hold up better under stress. Don't downgrade if your truck came with LT tires.

All-terrain vs highway: An all-terrain tread handles loose surfaces better, but adds road noise and wears faster on pavement. A highway all-season is quieter, more fuel-efficient, and longer-lasting for drivers who stick to city streets and the highway. For most Calgary RAM 1500 owners, a highway all-season is the practical call unless you're regularly off-road.

Brands like Michelin, Bridgestone, Goodyear, Continental, and Toyo all make solid LT-rated all-season options for the RAM 1500. Browse what we stock in our light truck tire collection.

Winter tires for the RAM 1500

Calgary winters are real. An all-season tire is not a winter tire — the rubber compound in an all-season hardens below 7°C, reducing grip at the exact moment you need it most. After a chinook drops overnight, refreezes a wet road, and you're on Deerfoot at 6 a.m., that difference is felt.

What to look for: the 3-Peak Mountain Snowflake symbol (3PMSF) on the sidewall. This means the tire has been independently tested for severe winter traction — not just marketed as a winter tire. All-season tires don't carry this rating. All-weather tires usually do, and they're a workable middle ground if you prefer one set year-round. For a full breakdown, our Calgary winter tire guide covers all three categories in plain terms.

Good winter tire choices for the RAM 1500 include the Michelin X-Ice Snow LT, Bridgestone Blizzak W965, Continental VanContact Ice, Toyo Observe GSi-6 HP, and Nexen Winguard WT1. Nexen and Toyo tend to land at a lower price point while still delivering real 3PMSF-rated performance in Calgary conditions.

The easiest setup for seasonal swapping: put your winter tires on a set of steel rims. Steel rims cost a fraction of alloys, protect your alloys from road salt, and make every changeover faster. We stock both winter tires and steel rims — you can bundle the whole package in one visit. Not sure what a seasonal changeover involves? Here's how it works.

Load ratings and towing: don't overlook them

The RAM 1500 can tow between 6,000 and 12,750 lb depending on the configuration. If you regularly pull a trailer or work the bed hard, your tires need to handle it. Load range tells you how much they can carry:

  • Load Range C (6-ply): Standard P-metric territory. Fine for unloaded daily use and light hauling.
  • Load Range D (8-ply): A good middle ground for most working RAM 1500s. Handles moderate towing and cargo.
  • Load Range E (10-ply): Maximum carrying capacity. Best for trucks that regularly tow near the upper end of the rating. Rides stiffer on an empty bed — that's the trade-off.

Your door jamb sticker shows the truck's GVWR (Gross Vehicle Weight Rating). Your tires' combined load capacity needs to exceed it. Don't downgrade — stepping up a load range is cheap insurance compared to the alternative.

How long do RAM 1500 tires last in Calgary?

Typical tire life on a RAM 1500 highway all-season: 60,000–80,000 km with regular rotation every 10,000–12,000 km. What shortens that:

  • Pothole season — Calgary's March and April are hard on tires. A hard impact can crack or bulge a sidewall without being obvious until the tire fails later
  • Heavy load cycling — regularly filling and emptying the bed stresses sidewalls differently than steady highway mileage
  • Running separate winter and summer sets — each set gets roughly half the annual mileage, so both last longer over time. This is a good problem to have.

The simple check: look for the wear indicator bars in the tread grooves. When they're flush with the tread surface, you're at the legal minimum. For a longer look at how Calgary conditions affect tread life, see How Long Do Tires Last in Calgary?

FAQ

Can I put P-metric tires on my RAM 1500 if it came with LT tires?

Technically yes, but you'll lower the load capacity. If you tow or carry meaningful loads, stick with LT-rated tires. If your RAM is a daily commuter with no regular cargo or trailer work, P-metric tires are fine and often less expensive. When in doubt, match or exceed the original spec.

Do I need to balance new tires when I install them?

Yes, always. A standard balance is part of every tire installation at Prince Tires. For big A/T or LT tires, you can upgrade to road force balancing for $15 per tire at our Edmonton Trail NE shop.

My TPMS light came on after I swapped to winter tires. What's happening?

Your RAM 1500's TPMS sensors are mounted inside the wheel, not the tire. If you moved to steel rims without sensors installed, the system lights up because it can't find them. The options: add TPMS sensors to the winter rims (the cleaner long-term fix) or have the system reset each season. We handle both at our TPMS sensor service.

What's the most affordable decent winter tire for a RAM 1500?

Nexen and Toyo both offer LT winter tire options that carry the 3-Peak Mountain Snowflake rating at a lower price than the premium European brands. You get real certified winter performance without the extra cost. We can walk you through the comparison in person.
